newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes up on unexpectedly bullish stock data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes up on unexpectedly bullish stock data.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices rose late Thursday on the back of unexpectedly bullish stock data, while grades were subdued in thin post Christmas trading.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) showed a drop of 5.16 million barrels in U.S. crude stocks, while distillate stocks were off by 1.89 million barrels.
Gasoline stocks were up by a slight 504,000 barrels, although the U.S. Energy Information Administration showed a draw of 300,000 barrels in a separate report issued today.
"Low inventories and the continuing stock draw would have to support crude prices," one trader said.
February West Texas Intermediate was trading around $25.05-15 a barrel, up five cents from Tuesday's cash market.
The Feb/Mar WTI spread widened considerably to around 85 cents, up 25 cents from Tuesday. WTI/Cushing Posting Plus changed hands at $2.44/45/46 cents.
Grade differentials remained thin through the close of the day. February WTI/Midland was talked at WTI/Cushing minus five cents to plus one cent, down one to five cents from Tuesday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James changed hands at 42 cents premium a barrel to WTI/Cushing, down three to eight cents from Tuesday.
The open transatlantic arbitrage has deflated domestic sweet prices, and further drops are expected. "I think you could see sweets come off another quarter," one trader said.
Sour grades were talked at a steady discount of minus $1.40-50 a barrel.
